The alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and lies well above the propodeal dorsum (Fig. 15). The propodeum bears a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. The metanotal groove is absent, and the metapleural lobes are conspicuous and triangular.

In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes downward posteriorly, forming a short posterior face. The anterior and dorsal surfaces of the postpetiole form a single convexity, and its posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view, both the petiole and postpetiole nodes are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5 to 7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. The rugae are irregular and tend to meander slightly, usually with a few anastomoses. The scrobal area is largely smooth but typically has 1 to 2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose; this sculpture extends around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured or bear only the faintest superficial traces of sculpture.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely covered with fine, acute hairs. Color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From it, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). For the leading-order solution, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms remain negligible, consistent with the mild-slope assumption. We therefore retained all the modified curvature terms neglected in the MSE to develop a uniform model.

We developed a numerical model using the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. The uniform model can generally predict salient features of waves over various sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, its results agree more closely with experimental data than those of other established models. For man-made bars, the results of both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than those of Kirby (1986).

The FEM model can also be applied to wave transformation over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

The myth of the Phaedrus is more intense than all previous descriptions, though it belongs to a distinct realm. It concerns a former existence rather than a future one, depicting a conflict between reason, aided by passion or righteous indignation, and the instincts of the animal within us. In that former life, the human soul travelled in the company of a god and perceived truth in the form of the universal before birth. Our present existence is the result of a struggle that took place beforehand.

This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, just as we ask where men were before birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" seems unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it is as influential and widespread as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is a figure of speech. The majesty and power of the whole passage, particularly the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can be rendered only inadequately in another language.

In the nervous system, transduction converts physical and chemical stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors convert these inputs into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

Mobile internet expands the possibilities of immersive storytelling through games played on portable, location-aware interfaces. It is the latest development in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that give players a role as both avatars in a gameworld and co-authors alongside its original designers.

Location-aware interfaces let players bring physical places into the gameworld and the gameworld into physical places, a first for interactive media. Mobile games also move away from linear narratives toward cooperative storytelling that draws on the player's experience of place.

The idea of the "author-player" as a worldmaker is not new. Mobile games extend it beyond the constraints of traditional video games by taking worldmaking off the screen and into the physical world. Location-aware interfaces make the player's sensory experience of real places part of the storytelling.

In this essay, we theorize the distinctive storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our attempt to use it in designing and implementing our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Few insects are as famous as the Glow-worm, a curious little animal that seems to celebrate life by lighting a lantern at its tail. Almost everyone knows its name, though few have seen it roaming the grass like a spark fallen from the full moon. The ancient Greeks called it the Bright-tailed; modern science knows it as *Lampyris*.

Fabre's *Book of Insects* is written specifically for children. Its texts are derived from Alexander Teixeira de Mattos's unabridged translations of the *Entomological Memoirs*, "retold" for young readers by Mrs. Rodolph Stawell, author of *Fairies I Have Met* and other works. She abridged and substantially revised them, if she did not outright bowdlerize them.

Subject: Tips for hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It includes many former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

The region has approximately five million inhabitants, making it significantly larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Although the area has a dense motorway network, hitchhiking can be difficult because of its complex network of smaller roads. The main motorways serving the region are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitchhike here, stay on these main motorways. The smaller roads can be extremely difficult to navigate, with very little transit traffic. Germany is generally a pleasant place to hitchhike, but the Ruhr Area is by far the most unpleasant part of the country for it. Hitchhiking within the region is comparable to hitchhiking in a big city like Istanbul: the cities are independent, but to travelers they can feel like districts of one massive city.

Best regards,

Subject: Study results: Lung tissue volume and aeration analysis

Dear Customer,

Our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes yielded the following findings.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as the number of voxels multiplied by the volume of each voxel, provided the compartment considered had a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was calculated as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between the same conditions.

We also calculated the change in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], each patient's distribution of lost lung aeration (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, or lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

We look forward to discussing these results with you.
